title: The Fourth That Returns — ensayo de claridad del clímax
instructions: The listener hears some tonal attacks as clumsy in the strongest passage. Make a conservative MUSICAL revision of the original, not a busier recomposition. Two private attempts failed: one constantly re-stated the subject and increased lead attacks from 30 to 52, reaching B6 instead of the original G6. Another increased second-violin notes from 10 to 28 and made it shadow the clarinet: Bb5 at 256.5 vs 256.75, D5 at 258 vs 258.5, F5 at 259.75 vs 260, D5 at 261 vs 261.5, with further C#4 taps near the end. Its explanation called that a dialogue, but the actual MIDI merely introduced repeated same pitches with tiny staggered offsets. Do not give another offset shadow or constant descending-scale imitation. All those attempts are REJECTED; the supplied MIDI is the ORIGINAL accepted starting point. Preserve the useful sparseness of the original answering violin and other worthwhile notes; there is no need to fill every part or to rewrite every gesture. The lead needs an intelligible sentence: expressive connected motion within phrases, longer structural notes reached with purpose, and breaths at actual phrase boundaries instead of small gaps after almost every note. Its original G6 peak at 240 should remain meaningful, with a prepared approach and an audible consequence, not be replaced by generic scales or a still higher climax. Secondary voices should make genuinely complementary gestures or support the main thought, not reattack the same pitches just after another voice. Some overlapping counterpoint and deliberate same-pitch reinforcement remain legitimate; this is not a ban on complexity, repeated notes or syncopation. Keep original register identity and rhythmic character, but let listeners follow who speaks, who answers, and what is sustained. Do not mechanically straighten timing, slow all parts, force everyone onto quarter notes, or replace all movement with pads. The unchanged accompaniment is authoritative: D minor at 224-232, C# diminished at 232-240, D Dorian at 240-256, Bb at 256-264, A7 at 264-272. Fit its actual notes and prepare/resolve any tension coherently. The original C#5 at 268 prepares the unchanged D-minor answer at 272 and is worth retaining. Preserve all material before 224, including bar 53, EXACTLY. Return complete parts for this interval; retaining an original note is entirely acceptable. Explain actual phrase linkage and complementary responses, not generic praise.
